families.label: Product dwell by visitor type
families.core_definition: Association between an aggregate product-page duration proxy and Revenue, including visitor-type interactions and nonlinear shape.
families.boundary_rationale: Per-page dwell variants and curve refinements share the same measured relation; they do not establish page-level dwell or causal effects.

families.label: Informational engagement by visitor type
families.core_definition: Whether the association between informational-page duration and Revenue differs by visitor type.
families.boundary_rationale: The focal page category and comparison differ from product-page dwell.

families.label: Weekend composition
families.core_definition: Whether observed weekend conversion differences persist after within-month standardization for visitor and traffic mix.
families.boundary_rationale: A calendar-group comparison, distinct from monthly outcome variation.

families.label: Monthly composition
families.core_definition: How much monthly Revenue-rate variation remains after standardizing visitor and traffic composition.
families.boundary_rationale: The contrast is month-to-month variation, not weekend versus weekday.

families.label: Count-duration measurement discordance
families.core_definition: Whether positive page counts paired with zero duration indicate a measurement pattern requiring event-level validation.
families.boundary_rationale: This audits measurement consistency rather than modeling purchase associations as the primary question.

families.label: PageValues predictive contribution
families.core_definition: How held-out Revenue prediction changes when PageValues is included or excluded.
families.boundary_rationale: PageValues-only, full-feature, no-PageValues, and month-held-out comparisons refine the same predictive contribution question.

families.label: Bounce and exit metrics
families.core_definition: Whether BounceRates and ExitRates provide distinct conditional predictive information about Revenue.
families.boundary_rationale: This compares two analytics metrics rather than PageValues or browsing duration.

families.label: Product-page depth composition
families.core_definition: How the low-versus-high product-page-count Revenue-rate difference changes after standardizing observed session context.
families.boundary_rationale: The focal contrast is page-count depth, not duration allocation or duration per page.

families.label: Product-duration allocation
families.core_definition: Whether product-page share of recorded category duration adds conditional or predictive information beyond browsing volume and page counts, including possible nonlinearity.
families.boundary_rationale: Share and allocation refinements concern the same composition measure; aggregate dwell per product page is a different measure.

families.label: Month-varying product-duration association
families.core_definition: Whether the conditional association between ProductRelated_Duration and Revenue varies across months.
families.boundary_rationale: The discriminating comparison is month-specific duration slopes, not duration share or visitor moderation.

families.label: SpecialDay and informational engagement
families.core_definition: Whether SpecialDay proximity modifies the informational-duration association with Revenue.
families.boundary_rationale: The focal relation is an interaction with informational browsing, not a general SpecialDay effect.

families.label: SpecialDay among no-information sessions
families.core_definition: Whether SpecialDay-associated Revenue differences among sessions with no informational views vary by visitor type.
families.boundary_rationale: This is a restricted-population calendar contrast, distinct from duration moderation.

families.label: SpecialDay beyond Month prediction
families.core_definition: Whether SpecialDay adds held-out predictive information beyond Month and supplied session context.
families.boundary_rationale: This tests incremental prediction, not within-month score contrasts or a browsing interaction.

families.label: SpecialDay within-month support
families.core_definition: Whether observed Month-by-SpecialDay support permits meaningful within-month Revenue comparisons.
families.boundary_rationale: The focus is estimability and observed overlap, not the size of a predictive or causal effect.

families.label: Informational-to-product sequence
families.core_definition: Whether returning to product pages after informational browsing is associated with purchase, conditional on comparable browsing volume.
families.boundary_rationale: This requires timestamped event sequences unavailable in the supplied aggregates.

families.label: Optional navigation aid experiment
families.core_definition: Whether offering an optional product-category navigation aid changes purchase completion in a randomized test.
families.boundary_rationale: The intervention is navigation support, distinct from product comparison or checkout disclosure.

families.label: Product comparison aid experiment
families.core_definition: Whether a product comparison aid changes purchase completion for eligible shoppers.
families.boundary_rationale: The intervention provides comparison information rather than general navigation support.

families.label: Delivery timing prompt experiment
families.core_definition: Whether displaying delivery dates and cutoff times changes purchase completion near special days.
families.boundary_rationale: This tests delivery-timing information, not product comparison or cost transparency.

families.label: Delivery cost disclosure experiment
families.core_definition: Whether showing estimated delivery cost before checkout changes purchase completion.
families.boundary_rationale: The manipulated information is cost disclosure, distinct from delivery timing.

records.reason: A defined visitor-type interaction, adjustment set, session unit, and failure condition make this a testable observational question; it appropriately limits causal interpretation.
Within-month rate comparison and common visitor/traffic standardization give a concrete contrast. The proposal correctly treats it as descriptive and flags overlap.
The count-duration discordance is measurable in the supplied rows, and the proposal distinguishes a descriptive audit from validation requiring timestamped events.
It defines observed and standardized monthly variation, a testable attenuation prediction, and the limits of descriptive standardization.
A held-out ablation directly tests PageValues' predictive contribution. The proposal correctly leaves decision-time availability unresolved without feature timestamps.

The computed interaction matches the specified model and shows a wide interval around zero. The revision reports uncertainty and does not claim absence or causal moderation; its independent-sample proposal is concrete.
records.needs_check: Independent replication requires a dataset with substantially more SpecialDay-proximate eligible sessions; no such sample is supplied.

records.reason: Matched held-out comparisons can test whether either analytics metric adds information conditional on the other and session activity. Metric interpretation remains appropriately limited.
The proposal precisely defines an aggregate proxy, visitor interaction, and adjustment. The computation timed out, and the record accurately leaves the forecast unevaluated with a workable next test.
records.needs_check: The interaction estimate and upper-tail sensitivity remain uncomputed because the supplied run timed out.

records.reason: The executed identical-fold ablation supports predictive contribution under the stated logistic pipeline. The record does not infer causation or prove PageValues is unavailable at decision time.
records.needs_check: Feature construction and availability before transaction completion remain undocumented.

records.reason: The ratio proxy and visitor interaction are explicit and testable; excluding PageValues and limiting claims to association are coherent choices.
This specifies the same SpecialDay-by-informational-duration contrast later tested in K006, with a clear subgroup, covariates, and noncausal interpretation.
The computation implements the stated quartile groups and shared-cell standardization, reports support and bootstrap uncertainty, and supports partial attenuation. The claim remains descriptive.
The final proposal specifies a share, paired evaluation, zero-duration handling, and a model-based contrast. No computation ran, and the record accurately presents this as untested.
records.needs_check: No model metrics or prevalence estimates were produced because dynamic execution was prohibited.

records.reason: The marginal-versus-standardized depth contrast and common-support restriction are clearly defined. It is a feasible observational decomposition, not a causal page-view effect.
It distinguishes time allocation from browsing volume and proposes a held-out contrast with explicit adjustment and observational scope.
The nonlinear proxy and visitor-type shape comparison are falsifiable and use available fields. Proxy interpretation and the exclusion of Other are stated.
The sequence contrast is meaningful and specifies event timestamps, session boundaries, and transaction timing needed to establish ordering; current aggregates cannot answer it.
The aggregate per-page proxy, visitor interaction, adjustment, and failure condition form a coherent observational test, with mechanism claims reserved for event data or randomization.
A fixed held-out comparison tests incremental SpecialDay prediction beyond Month and context. The proposal limits conclusions to one-year within-dataset evidence.
The within-month categorical contrast is concrete and flags sparse score-by-month cells. It correctly avoids treating Month adjustment as causal identification.
The counts support the stated overlap limitation, and the revision no longer treats model predictions under unsupported score assignments as observed contrasts. It is a scoped feasibility result.
records.needs_check: No prespecified precision threshold defines adequate support, so the result establishes sparse support rather than a formal estimability boundary.

records.reason: This is the same timestamped informational-to-product return question as K017, with a clear volume-adjusted comparison and necessary event data.
The restricted population and visitor-specific SpecialDay contrast are explicit and falsifiable. Calendar proximity is not misrepresented as randomized exposure.
Holding out each Month is a temporal robustness refinement of the PageValues ablation, with shared pipeline and clear limits on decision-time interpretation.
A randomized, persistent shopper-level assignment and intention-to-treat purchase outcome provide a concrete causal test beyond these observational aggregates.
Eligibility precedes assignment, the intervention and transaction window are specified, and repeat visitors are handled by persistent assignment.
The computed eligibility and decile summaries justify refining the question to nonlinear association, but they do not establish one. The final proposal correctly calls for adjusted held-out testing.
records.needs_check: Conditional overlap for the proposed adjusted model was not established by the returned marginal summaries.

records.reason: The fitted model and cap sensitivity support a dataset-specific difference in proxy curve shape and reverse the original New_Visitor forecast. The revision labels this observational and awaits replication.
records.needs_check: Uncertainty intervals for the group-specific slopes and combined New_Visitor curvature were not returned.

records.reason: It specifies a randomized delivery-timing prompt, eligible population, purchase outcome, and assignment persistence. The required live-site measurements are explicit.
The comparison aid and high-dwell eligibility are explicit, with dwell measured before assignment and a subgroup-effect prediction. A live experiment is necessary.
The paired cross-validation result supports a small mean predictive gain, while the record acknowledges mixed folds, limited SpecialDay support, and lack of independent replication.
records.needs_check: No uncertainty interval for the conditional incremental gain was computed; folds reuse observations and do not provide independent replications.

records.reason: The product-duration-per-page proxy is testable with the available fields, and the proposal states its measurement and noncausal limitations.
This is a concrete PageValues ablation with held-out performance and calibration, while correctly separating predictive dependence from causality and feature availability.
The disclosure intervention, pre-randomization eligibility, assignment unit, and required event measurements are specified clearly enough for a live randomized test.
It tests product-duration allocation conditional on total duration and page counts, explicitly states the required duration comparability assumption, and excludes PageValues.
The shared-versus-month-varying duration association is a concrete held-out comparison. Campaign and date context are correctly identified as needed for interpretation.

cross_record_observations: K008, K010, K016, K018, K028, and K032 share the aggregate product-duration proxy by visitor type; K016 and K028 refine this to nonlinear shape.
K006 and K011 test SpecialDay moderation of informational-duration association. K006 reports a near-zero, highly uncertain estimate and appropriately retains the question as unresolved.
K012 and K014 compare product-page-depth conversion differences before and after context standardization; K012 supplies the computed result.
K013, K015, K027, and K035 concern product-page duration allocation. K027's marginal deciles motivate a nonlinear proposal but do not establish an adjusted association.
K005, K009, K024, and K033 examine PageValues predictive contribution; K024 adds month-held-out evaluation. K009 reports a clear within-benchmark ablation, not decision-time validity.
K019 and K031 test SpecialDay's incremental predictive value beyond Month; K031 finds a small mean gain with mixed folds. K020 and K021 instead concern within-month support.
K017 and K022 require event-sequence data absent from the supplied aggregates. K025-K030 and K034 propose distinct randomized interventions with explicit assignment and outcome plans.
